title: Port E-001..E-006's acceptance checks (the 14 ledger finish bodies, 6 of them Python, and run_finish_e004_2's look assertions) to Go tests that build and drive the real program over HTTP
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

Open(t), which calls Browser, against Open(tb, browser), which re-checks isEdge. Open(t) was chosen because it is structurally impossible to misuse. Crossdomain's version matched Shot's existing signature.
The E-004 browser checks as their own top-level test (practice) against subtests named 'E004 …' of one test on a shared loopback program (crossdomain).

Mapping location: tests/acceptance/ported_test.go at the root package (practice), against tests/acceptance/disposition (crossdomain), against tests/acceptance/ported/ (chosen).

deviation: The ported package is test-only: attempt 1's non-test tests/acceptance/ported/ported.go is renamed ported_test.go, the table is in rows_test.go and the checks in check_test.go. The design named ported_test.go, and the stack line says tests/acceptance holds test-only packages.

deviation: New package internal/testutil/outside, which is not in the design's component list. It is the single mustBeOutsideModule helper that the m4 critic prescribed, used by both program and headless. headless now imports it.

deviation: New build-tagged package tests/acceptance/suite (TestSuiteWithoutABrowser, TestSuiteInChrome). The design's C1/C2 check commands were PowerShell text matches, which M-add-3's decision replaced with -json event parsing; this package gives those cases a command with no shell syntax. Rule 4 excepts tests/acceptance/suite/**, because the package removes CHROME_BIN from, or passes it into, the inner go test; it starts and chooses no browser.

deviation: Rule 4 bans the words CHROME_BIN and HBAND_TEST_BROWSER anywhere in tests/acceptance, not only inside Getenv("..."), so os.Environ scans and backquotes are caught. A bare 'chrome' cannot be banned, because the verbatim E-001/E-002 bodies use it for their User-Agent; this is a named hole.

deviation: The tag-placement rule accepts a tag on the line of, or the line just above, a checking statement, or on the first line of the block that the line below opens (an if, for or case). The critic's text said only 'same line or line just above'; without the extra allowance, a check written as `if cond { t.Fatalf }` could not be tagged.

deviation: The def-call propagation the critic prescribed for Sites flags name collisions as sites: in the E-004 line 2 body, built-in open() and read() share names with Chrome.open/Chrome.read, at L58, L118, L181, L207, L208, L318 and L319. Each such line has a row saying so. Those inside the stand-in GitHub are Helper rows to fakegithub; the others are Superseded 'not an assertion', or Ported to headless.Open where they are the DevToolsActivePort read.

deviation: seedBody (the E-004 line 2 body's posting and HTTP checks) runs in both E-004 line 2 tests. The browser test therefore re-makes the HTTP checks on loopback http before its Chrome checks. The production-shaped https run is TestE004DeepThreadsAndBranchPages.

deviation: The Go Visitor does not imitate the Python Browser's extras: a Chrome User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For 192.0.2.10, CSRF hidden fields and Origin on every post. hband has no CSRF tokens, CrossOriginProtection accepts requests with no Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site, and no E-003..E-006 assertion depends on User-Agent or forwarded address. Anonymous and blocked-account posts use Post without following, where the Python followed hband's redirects up to the stand-in; those sites assert only status < 500.

drift: internal/testutil/program grew three files that are not in the design's component list (program.go, visitor.go, thread.go, program_test.go) and not under the build's deviations: - reader.go: the Python prelude's page readers (Count, Vote, Dislikes, Say, Part, Visible, Shown, Own, Depth, Mine), with ported tags; - html.go: a second forgiving HTML tree (Node/Dom), beside internal/testutil/e002row's Node/Dom; - expect.go: Expect, ExpectEq, Mark, Account, Report, Resolve. The two Dom parsers port different readers: e002row strips script and style, while html.go keeps script text as raw text, which E41-393 needs. Keeping both is defensible, but a later reader should know there are two.
